title: Cross-system swivel-chair elimination: provenance-tracked translation of plans, targets and intelligence products between planning, fires, airspace, intel and briefing systems (Onebrief/COP graphics to AFATDS/AXS, TAIS, IBCS-M; AIDP/DCGS-A to MSS, chat and slides)
problem: Plans, targets and intelligence products are authored in one environment (Onebrief, PowerPoint, MSS/AIDP, chat) and re-keyed by staff officers and analysts into the specialized systems that execute or brief them (AFATDS/AXS, TAIS, IBCS-M, COP, INTSUM slides), so every battle-rhythm cycle burns staff hours on manual reconciliation and the resulting products carry no machine-readable provenance or releasability lineage.

user.exact_role: Fires cell (FSO/FSNCO, 13A/13J), ADAM/BAE airspace cell, current-operations battle captain, and 35F/35G all-source analysts and targeting officers who today hand-carry data between planning, fires, airspace, intel and briefing systems
user.echelon: Brigade through corps, with a second user population at COCOM J2/J3 targeting cells
organization_examples: 4th Infantry Division and 25th Infantry Division (NGC2 prototype divisions)
XVIII Airborne Corps (Scarlet Dragon targeting cell)
III Armored Corps / I Corps (next NGC2 recipients)
CENTCOM and INDOPACOM J2/J3 targeting cells using Maven Smart System
Army National Guard division/brigade staffs using AFATDS/TAIS with legacy CPCE

current_workflow: 1. Planners build the scheme of maneuver, fire support plan and airspace coordination measures in Onebrief and/or PowerPoint/Excel; intel builds the enemy picture in MSS/AIDP and slides.
2. The fires cell re-enters targets, target lists and fire support coordination measures into AFATDS (or the new AXS microservices) by hand from the plan graphics.
3. The ADAM/BAE cell re-enters airspace coordination measures into TAIS and coordinates changes with aviation and air defense (IBCS-M) by chat and phone.
4. Analysts receive cues from Maven/AIDP, chat and email, verify in an imagery tool, then manually build target graphics and INTSUM slides and re-type entity data into fires C2 and the COP.
5. Any change in one system is re-keyed into the others; sustainment status arrives by spreadsheet/LOGSTAT.

6. Discrepancies between systems are discovered at rehearsals, during live fire, or when a target nomination is rejected; provenance of who changed what and from which source is reconstructed from chat logs after the fact.
current_solution: Humans plus liaison officers plus chat (Teams/Mattermost/mIRC) plus contractor field service engineers; inside the NGC2 prototypes the data layer (Anduril Lattice, Palantir Foundry, Raft registries/transformation/federation) and Raft's voice/AI workflows, a Lockheed/Accelint unified airspace interface and Maven's target workbench routing to AFATDS/JREAP are being demonstrated exercise-by-exercise; Onebrief claims its plans are 'pushed into the specialized systems that execute them' (vendor claim); OSD is forcing analytic tools onto MSS as the top-down consolidation answer.
failure: The seam fails at the semantic and safety boundary: fires and airspace systems require validated, doctrinally checked, auditable message content (VMF/USMTF/JREAP semantics, fire support coordination measures, ACMs), legacy programs of record exposed usable APIs only in May 2026 (Operation Jailbreak), the NGC2 integrations are prototype-specific to one division's vendor stack, and the intel-to-briefing side loses provenance and releasability markings the moment a product becomes a slide or a chat message.

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons. (1) Until Operation Jailbreak (May 2026) the programs of record on the execution side (AFATDS, TAIS, IBCS-M, GCSS-Army) had no documented, vendor-accessible APIs; interface control documents and VMF/USMTF/JREAP implementations are CUI/export-controlled, so only the fires-C2 developer (Leidos on AFATDS; the AXS microservice vendors) and the NGC2 team leads could touch the seam. (2) The seam is now explicitly assigned: the Army's June 2026 NGC2 common data baseline gives Anduril/Palantir/Raft the registries, transformation and federation layer, Onebrief holds the planning layer, and OSD's April 2026 MSS directive gives Palantir the intel-product target - the 'translation' job is on the incumbents' roadmap and funded through their OTAs and enterprise agreements. (3) The fires/airspace side requires safety-authority acceptance (a wrong ACM or FSCM translation is a fratricide risk), and the intel side requires classified data to make products realistic; both are gated for a small uncleared team. Startups that got close (Raft, Onebrief, Vannevar) did so as team members inside a prime's OTA, not as standalone translation products.
technical_wedge: Not the whole seam. The only defensible slice for a newcomer is a narrow, auditable transformation-and-provenance service for ONE mission thread: e.g., (a) plan/COP graphics (Onebrief JSON, MIL-STD-2525 overlays, ACO/ATO products) to validated airspace coordination measures and fire support coordination measures with doctrinal conflict detection, human approval gates and a per-object provenance ledger; or (b) an intel-product generator that turns structured detections/tracks plus chat into standard, machine-readable products (USMTF/VMF messages, CoT, INTSUM sections, target packets) with per-claim source lineage and releasability markings. Packaged as a registered service/app in the NGC2 registry or an Open DAGIR/MSS app rather than as a competing platform.

mvp.what: An unclassified 'translation with receipts' service: ingest an Onebrief-style plan export or 2525 overlay plus simulated detections and chat, emit validated ACM/FSCM sets and target nominations as CoT and mock VMF/USMTF messages into a TAK server and a mock AFATDS message endpoint, with a provenance graph (who/what/when/source) and doctrinal conflict flags; round-trip changes back to the plan.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the unclassified simulation: open TAK/CoT, public MIL-STD-2525 and public USMTF/ADatP-3 structure, synthetic exercise data; measurable analyst/fires-cell time saved with 3-5 veteran 13A/35F advisors on a scripted scenario; cannot demonstrate against real AFATDS/TAIS/IBCS-M without a government sponsor and CUI interface docs.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That (1) automated translation reduces re-keying time and error rate versus the manual baseline on realistic products, (2) every emitted object carries verifiable lineage and releasability, (3) conflict detection catches seeded ACM/FSCM errors, and (4) the government sponsor (a fires or intel cell) will accept the human-approval workflow as safe enough to try at an exercise.

data_requirement.what: Plan and product templates (OPORD annexes, fire support plans, ACO/ACM formats, INTSUM/target packet templates), message-format specifications (VMF, USMTF, JREAP-C, CoT), unit SOPs and realistic chat logs for evaluation; eventually PoR interface control documents.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: Partially. MIL-STD-2525, CoT/TAK and public STANAG/ADatP-3 structures are open; USMTF/VMF and AFATDS/TAIS/IBCS-M ICDs are CUI and export-controlled (needs a government sponsor, a U.S.-person team for the controlled portion, and counsel on ITAR/EAR handling); realistic chat logs and INTSUMs are CUI or classified, so evaluation data must be synthetic or sponsor-provided.

entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR requires >50% ownership and control by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (13 CFR 121.702) - the German founder qualifies only after obtaining permanent residency, and the Indonesian founder's stake counts against the threshold; foreign-affiliation disclosure is mandatory. OTAs/CSOs have no statutory ownership test. Export-controlled CUI (message-format ICDs) is effectively U.S.-person-only, so the non-U.S.-person founder may be walled off from the core interface work; FOCI treats any non-citizen, including a permanent resident, as a foreign interest for facility clearance. All of this needs export-control and government-contracts counsel before the first sponsor conversation.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, easily and they are already doing it: Anduril/Palantir/Raft hold the NGC2 transformation layer, Palantir holds MSS and the intel side, Onebrief holds the plan; the Army's Jailbreak program lowers their integration cost every quarter. Leidos/AXS vendors can expose the fires interface natively.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: Mostly reject as a standalone company. The only credible residual is a narrow, safety-auditable transformation/provenance service that the primes have little incentive to build well (validation rules, lineage, releasability), sold as a component inside the baseline or as an Open DAGIR app - a feature-sized business with thin margins, not a platform. A startup wins only if it becomes the neutral, government-owned-data-rights 'audit and validation' layer that the Army wants to keep independent of any one prime; that is a plausible but unproven procurement preference.

capital_required.assumptions: PoC: 2 founders plus 1-2 veteran advisors, unclassified TAK/CoT simulation, 6 months. Demo: 5-8 people including a cleared U.S.-person integration lead and a former FSO/35F, one exercise cycle under a team-lead subcontract, CUI-capable environment, 12-18 months. Production: IL5/SIPR hosting or Open DAGIR onboarding, security assessment (the NGC2 CTO memo of Sept 2025 shows third-party apps get audited), sustained field-service engineers at two divisions, 24-36 months. Figures are INFERENCE from comparable C2-app startups; no public evidence for this specific product.

regulatory_burden.explanation: The product's value depends on CUI/export-controlled interface specifications for fires and air-defense C2 (VMF/USMTF ICDs, AFATDS/TAIS/IBCS-M APIs) and on realistic data that is CUI or classified; fires automation triggers safety-authority review; deployment requires NGC2 security assessment or Open DAGIR/IL5 onboarding; ITAR 'specially designed' analysis is needed once the software is built for USML-controlled fire-control/air-defense systems (describe, do not conclude - counsel required).
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: The Indonesian founder (not a U.S. person) cannot receive export-controlled technical data or CUI marked export-controlled without a license/TAA, would be walled off from the core integration work, counts against the SBIR >50% U.S.-ownership test, and is a 'foreign interest' for any facility clearance under 32 CFR 117.11; the German founder is treated as a U.S. person under ITAR only after lawful permanent residency (22 CFR 120.62) but remains a foreign interest for FOCI purposes. Company structure, role separation and a technology control plan need counsel before sponsor engagement.

dual_use_potential.explanation: The doctrinal semantics (FSCMs, ACMs, VMF/USMTF, target packets) have no commercial analogue; the generic pieces (provenance ledgers, schema translation, LLM product generation) are commoditized in the enterprise market. Only the allied-military market (FMN/STANAG-native translation for NATO land forces, where the German founder has access) is a second market, and it is military, not commercial.

defensibility.explanation: Defensibility would come from validated, accredited transformation rules per mission thread and from being the registered service inside the NGC2/Open DAGIR baselines that units have trained on; none of this is protected by IP, all of it is contestable by the baseline holders, and government-purpose data rights on OTA-funded adapters limit lock-in. Weak.

why_now: (1) Legacy Army PoRs exposed documented APIs for the first time in May 2026 (Operation Jailbreak, >70 capabilities, ~80 vendors) with an API marketplace and Jailbreak 1.5 planned; (2) the Army set a common NGC2 data baseline in June 2026 and plans reuse of apps across 11 divisions and 4 corps by FY2032; (3) OSD's April 2026 MSS directive defines a single API target for intel products; (4) AXS re-architects fires C2 as microservices and demonstrated live fire in 2026; (5) LLM-based structured-product generation with citations became credible in 2025-2026. Together these make provenance-tracked translation technically possible and procurable for the first time - but they benefit incumbents at least as much as newcomers.
killer_risk: The seam is already assigned and funded: Anduril/Palantir/Raft own the NGC2 transformation layer, Onebrief owns the plan, Palantir owns MSS, Leidos/AXS vendors own the fires interface, and the Army's own Jailbreak program is doing the API plumbing - so a two-student startup with one non-U.S.-person founder, no clearances and no access to export-controlled ICDs would be building a feature the baseline holders can ship first, for a customer who has just consolidated onto their platforms.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling, for a different reason: allied land forces run on FMN Spiral 4/5, MIP/JC3IEDM, ADatP-3 and STANAG 4677, which are published or obtainable standards, and NATO DEMETER (Systematic SitaWare) plus MSS NATO create the same plan-to-execution and intel-to-product seams with less classification friction and a German founder who can access national and NATO DIANA channels. Balikatan 2026 shows coalition COP releasability is still hand-tagged, which is exactly the provenance/releasability feature. But the allied 'interoperability layer' slot is held by Systematic and Palantir, CWIX/Bold Quest are the proving grounds (cheap to enter, slow to monetize), and an EU-only instrument may be constrained by third-country control with an Indonesian co-founder. Net: allied market improves access and reduces classification dependence but does not change the feature-not-company verdict.
